newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt welcomes "new" U.S. position on Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Egypt welcomes "new" U.S. position on Mideast peace.

text.p: Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on Thursday welcomed U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's call on Israel and the Palestinians to avoid unilateral measures and work as partners for peace.

Albright, speaking on Wednesday, one week after a twin suicide bombing in Jerusalem, said she planned to go to the Middle East at the end of August, provided the security situation improved, to try to speed up work on "final status" talks for Israeli-Palestinian peace.

"Madeleine Albright articulated a certain new American position concerning the process...," Moussa told reporters after attending a meeting between Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan.
"The articulation of an initiative along those lines by the United States is very important as the sponsor of the peace process," he added.

Albright said: "We seek a just and lasting peace achieved through direct negotiations, based on U.N. Security Council resolutions 242 and 338, including the principle on which every Arab-Israeli agreement has been built: land for peace."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has indicated his hostility to the land for peace formula upon which peace talks were launched between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.

Moussa said Albright's comments were a call for "a just and lasting peace and equal commitment, obligations and rights. The balanced approach is what we all need to meet the requirements of peace and the aspirations of those parties to a just and lasting peace".

"On the Palestininan-Israeli track she was very clear that in addition to security, important as it is, it is equally important that no unilateral measures be undertaken because those measures undermine the future of the peace process.

"She demanded the commitment of both parties as partners to work together in order to implement the agreements that have been reached and work within the framework of resolutions 242 and 338 -- the principle of land for peace, the principle of comprehensive and lasting and just peace in the Middle East.
The twin suicide bombing in a crowded west Jerusalem market last week that killed 15 people, including the two bombers, pushed Middle East peace efforts to their gloomiest state in months.

Israel suspended a resumption of talks with the Palestinians and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza after the explosions, preventing thousands of Palestinians from going to work in Israel and freezing the transfer of VAT and customs duties it owes the Palestinian Authority.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was quoted on Thursday as saying the measures Israel imposed on the Palestinians after the bombing amounted to a declaration of war, and warned that he was preparing accordingly.

Egypt and Jordan, the only two Arab states which have peace agreements with Israel, have led diplomatic efforts to ease the latest crisis ahead of a visit to the region by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross at the end of this week.
